newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt, India's Cadila in pact.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt, India's Cadila in pact.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc said Tuesday it had signed a five-year sales and marketing pact with Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd of India.
The alliance is expected to produce $150 million in annual sales by 2002, Mallinckrodt said.

Under the pact, Mallinckrodt and Cadila will jointly sell, market, distribute, research and develop, and manufacture various products in the United States, India and other worldwide markets, Mallinckrodt said.
"Technology development and international business development are central to Mallinckrodt's integrated growth plan," said Mallinckrodt Chairman and Chief Executive C. Ray Holman.

"This partnership with Cadila, which has strong market positions in India, Russia and Africa and a solid technology base in pharmaceuticals and hospital products, will give us a platform for growth in India as well as other important Asia Pacific and global markets," Holman said.
The five-year pact is renewable, the company said.

Mallinckrodt did not disclose specific products or product lines to be incorporated in the agreement, but the companies said in a joint statement they expected their medical products, pharmaceuticals and laboratory chemicals businesses to benefit from the pact.

Initial agreements were expected to include distribution of Mallinckrodt products in India and Cadila products in the United States, and packaging, sterilization and other manufacturing processes of Mallinckrodt products by Cadila in India, the companies said.

"We expect this alliance to be a long-lasting one that will evolve over time and anticipate that there may be an exchange of personnel between Mallinckrodt and Cadila to support the achievement of our goals," Holman said.

Cadila Pharmaceuticals Chairman I. A. Modi said, "Our manufacturing and formulation development expertise will serve as a strong base for Mallinckrodt to rapidly and cost effectively introduce generic formulations into the U.S. market."
